newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to adopt mobile technology communication.
newsitem.headline: Commission to adopt mobile technology communication.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to adopt a communication on Thursday on ways to promote the next generation of mobile communications technology.

The paper will address questions related to the Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS), a technology that will allow consumers to carry out a range of data and video communications over small "personal communicators".

"The key issue is, how do we ensure that Europe's industry, which has had a big success with GSM, stays competitive in the future -- and how do we ensure users' needs are addressed as well," a Commission official told Reuters.
European companies developed the GSM global digital mobile phone standard, which allows consumers to use their phone across Europe.

The Commission paper will ask how such "pan-European roaming" can be extended to multimedia services, the official said. It will also address issues including standards, frequencies and the regulatory framework.
"Do we need regulation and what is the right moment?" he said.
The communication will resemble a "green paper" in that it will ask interested parties to comment on key questions related to promoting the industry, the official said.

The Commission announced in February it was working with European companies to develop a strategy for introducing UMTS. It said industry leaders told it they needed a stable regulatory environment, including licensing conditions and dedicated frequency allocations.
It said a key role would be played by the UMTS Forum, which unites manufacturers, cellular and satellite communications operators, regulators and others.
